title: How people use water
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the basic idea of how people use water in everyday life, farming, industry and electricity; the closest, Competing uses of water, is about uses clashing in dry years, which is a different and narrower idea.

draft.title: How people use water
card: People use water every day for drinking, cooking and washing. Many also use it to water gardens.
Farmers use water to grow crops and to give drinking water to livestock. Watering crops is called irrigation.
Factories and mines use water to clean, cool and process things. Water is also an ingredient in some products, such as drinks.
Water is used to make electricity. Falling water can turn machines called turbines in hydroelectric power stations.
draft.remember: Water is used at home, in farming, in industry and to make electricity.

a.q: A farmer near Griffith pumps water onto her rice crop. Which use of water is this?
a.why: Giving water to crops is irrigation, which is a farming use. Industry means factories and mines, which is a different use, even though the water is still used to make a product.
a.clue: Think about what the water is helping to grow.

b.q: At a hydroelectric power station in the Snowy Mountains, falling water turns turbines. What is the water being used for?
b.why: Falling water turns turbines, and this makes electricity. Cooling a factory is an industry use, but the water here is not cooling anything.
